title: The Flavians and the Colosseum
objective: After this level you can describe the Flavian dynasty and the building of the Colosseum.
summary: Vespasian and his sons Titus and Domitian ruled until 96 CE. They built the Colosseum on the grounds of Nero’s palace.

cards.headline: The Colosseum stands where an emperor’s private lake used to be.
A family of soldiers
cards.body: In 70 CE Vespasian’s son Titus captured Jerusalem and destroyed its Temple. Titus succeeded Vespasian and was followed by his brother Domitian, whose harsh rule ended with his murder in 96 CE.

cards.headline: The Colosseum
cards.body: Vespasian began the Colosseum, and Titus opened it in 80 CE with games that lasted 100 days. It could hold about 50,000 spectators. It stood on the site of a lake in the grounds of Nero’s Golden House, giving the land back to public use.

cards.fact: The Colosseum’s real name was the Flavian Amphitheatre.
cards.context: The name Colosseum came later, probably from a colossal statue of Nero that stood nearby.

cards.headline: The Colosseum: opened
learned: It was built on Nero’s palace grounds

questions.prompt: About how many spectators could the Colosseum hold?
Why did building on Nero’s palace grounds send a message?

options.label: It hid the damage from the Great Fire
It gave a hated ruler’s land back to the people
It honored Nero as the Flavians’ ancestor
It was the only flat land left in Rome

questions.explanation: Turning Nero’s private lake into a public arena showed the new dynasty sharing Rome with its people.

questions.prompt: From Level 54: what had Nero built on land cleared by the Great Fire?

options.label: A temple to the god Janus
A new wall around the city
A vast palace, the Golden House
A harbor for the grain ships

questions.explanation: Nero built the Golden House on land cleared by the fire; the Flavians built the Colosseum on its grounds.
